content: Several co‑owners (two spouses and others) asked for dissolution and division of land and buildings; the Court‑Appointed Expert proposed lots (Q1, Q2, Q3) with equalizations. The main interpretive question was allocation criteria among co‑owners and discretionary departure from drawing lots. The court framed division to preserve ongoing business use (butcher shop), assigning that asset to the operator spouse to avoid disruption. Principles: drawing lots is not mandatory; objective and subjective opportunity may justify direct assignment; equalizations are secured by legal mortgage; expert costs apportioned. Partial costs awarded against opposing defendants. 1.
